Nuevo Laredo Mayor Carmen Lilia Canturosas Villarreal delivered five paving and repaving projects backed by an investment of more than 31.7 million pesos, modernizing the city's road network, according to Tamaulipas Literal.

Together, the projects cover more than 15,900 square meters of roadways, with hydraulic concrete and asphalt paving, new public lighting, renewed water and sewer lines, and improvements meant to strengthen mobility and safety for thousands of families, according to the report.

The largest of the five is the repaving of San Salomón street, both east and west sections, at 7,983,537 pesos across 2,465 square meters, built for greater durability and better driving conditions, according to the report.

Repaving on Abraham Lincoln street cost 5,559,695 pesos and covered 8,278 square meters through patching and recycled asphalt, restoring driving conditions on the busy roadway, according to the report. Repaving on Habana street cost 5,386,442 pesos across 1,742 square meters, including new sidewalks, public lighting and renewed household water and sewer connections, and improved access to Secondary School No. 5.

Asphalt paving on Azucena street cost 4,404,476 pesos across 1,768 square meters, with curbs, sidewalks, signage and public lighting, improving the connection between two sectors of the city without requiring drivers to go to the National Highway, according to the report.

Repaving with hydraulic concrete on Matehuala street in the Palmares neighborhood cost 4,217,070 pesos across 1,726 square meters, including replacement of household water and sewer connections, new sidewalks, improved roadbeds and signage, according to the report.

The same infrastructure day also delivered a new public lighting network along Boulevard Universidad, at 4,221,821 pesos across 1,980 linear meters, improving visibility and safety in that area of the city, according to the report.

Canturosas Villarreal said her administration is showing that when there is a will to work and manage public resources responsibly, cities can be transformed, and she said the city will keep investing in its streets.

Sources: Tamaulipas Literal.

title: Nuevo Laredo Delivers Five Road Projects in 31.7-Million-Peso Investment
